(Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | construction_period = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National Important Cultural Properties. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and Important Cultural Properties > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National Important Cultural Properties in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National Important Cultural Properties on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | construction_period = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National Important Cultural Properties. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and Important Cultural Properties > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National Important Cultural Properties in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National Important Cultural Properties on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | construction_period = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National Important Cultural Properties. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and Important Cultural Properties > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National Important Cultural Properties in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National Important Cultural Properties on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). Shibagahara Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' - Designated June 29, 1990{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|Artifacts from Shibagahara Kofun}}. === National Historic Site === * '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | construction_period = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National Important Cultural Properties. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and Important Cultural Properties > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National Important Cultural Properties in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National Important Cultural Properties on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | construction_period = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National Important Cultural Properties. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and Important Cultural Properties > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National Important Cultural Properties in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National Important Cultural Properties on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | construction_period = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National Important Cultural Properties. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and Important Cultural Properties > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National Important Cultural Properties in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National Important Cultural Properties on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). Shibagahara Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' - Designated June 29, 1990{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}. === National Historic Site === * '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}. == Related Facilities == * '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National Important Cultural Properties. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and Important Cultural Properties > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National Important Cultural Properties in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National Important Cultural Properties on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 装身具.JPG|Ornaments File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 庄内式土器.JPG|Shōnai-style pottery == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Property (National Designation) === * '''Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' - Designated June 29, 1990{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}. === National Historic Site === * '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}. == Related Facilities == * '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun part_of|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National Important Cultural Properties. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun part_of|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and Important Cultural Properties > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National Important Cultural Properties in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National Important Cultural Properties on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National Important other_designation. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and Important other_designation > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National Important other_designation in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National Important other_designation on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 装身具.JPG|Ornaments File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 庄内式土器.JPG|Shōnai-style pottery == other_designation == === Important Cultural Property (National Designation) === * '''Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' - Designated June 29, 1990{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}. === National Historic Site === * '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}. == Related Facilities == * '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada Imahoricho, Joyo (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National Important other_designation. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and Important other_designation > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National Important other_designation in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National Important other_designation on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its artifacts are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National other_designation (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National other_designation, and its artifacts are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National other_designation)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National other_designation)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National other_designations and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National other_designation in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National other_designation on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National other_designation)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National other_designation)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National other_designation)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial_chamber = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | artifacts = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | designation = National other_designation (Shibagahara Kofun) | cultural_property = Artifacts designated as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | label = Shibagahara Kofun | marker = 前方後方墳-南 | label_position = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National other_designation, and its artifacts are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National other_designation)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National other_designation)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National other_designations and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was designated a National other_designation in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were designated National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National other_designation on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National other_designation)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == Artifacts == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major artifacts recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National other_designation)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Information No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National other_designation)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).
