(Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | Historic Site = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | omitted = 前方後方墳-南 | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | Historic Site = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | omitted = 前方後方墳-南 | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 装身具.JPG|Ornaments File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 庄内式土器.JPG|Shōnai-style pottery == Historic Site == === Important Cultural Property (National Designation) === * '''burial goods Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' - Designated June 29, 1990{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}. === National Historic Site === * '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}. == Related Facilities == * '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada Imahoricho, Joyo City) - Houses and exhibits burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun. == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|Sources used for article composition}} * Historic Site Description Board. * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2007|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun|title={{PDFlink|[http://www.kyotofu-maibun.or.jp/data/kankou/kankou-pdf/jyouhou/J104.pdf Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104]}}|publisher=Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Research Center|isbn=|pages=36-37|ref={{Harvid|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007}}}}. == Related Literature == {{small|References not used for article composition}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=Seigo Wada|year=1989|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[Tōkyōdō Shu11an]]|isbn=4490102607|ref=}}. * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1987|chapter=|title=Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo City Archaeological Report No. 16)|publisher=Joyo City Board of Education|isbn=|ref=}}. * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2014|chapter=|title=Shibagahara Kofun Excavation and Preservation Report (Joyo City Archaeological Report No. 68)|publisher=Joyo City Board of Education|isbn=|ref=}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo)}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} of Kyoto Prefecture]] {{Kofun navbar}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:Kutsukawa Kofun Group]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Joyo]] [[Category:Zenpō-kōhō-fun]] [[Category:[[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] [[Category:National Historic Sites of Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Shiba-Gahara Kofun]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:New2]] }} [[sn:Shibagahara Kofun]] [[ja:芝ヶ原古墳]] [[sn:hibagahara Kofun]]

(Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|12=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | Historic Site = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | omitted = 前方後方墳-南 | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|12=draft}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=draft}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|12=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | Historic Site = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | omitted = 前方後方墳-南 | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|12=draft}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=draft}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=draft}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|12=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | Historic Site = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | omitted = 前方後方墳-南 | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|12=draft}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=draft}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|12=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | Historic Site = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | omitted = 前方後方墳-南 | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|12=draft}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=draft}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 装身具.JPG|Ornaments File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 庄内式土器.JPG|Shōnai-style pottery == Historic Site == === Important Cultural Property (National Designation) === * '''burial goods Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' - Designated June 29, 1990{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}. === National Historic Site === * '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}. == Related Facilities == * '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada Imahoricho, Joyo Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 装身具.JPG|Ornaments File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 庄内式土器.JPG|Shōnai-style pottery == Historic Site == === Important Cultural Property (National Designation) === * '''burial goods Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' - Designated June 29, 1990{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}. === National Historic Site === * '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}. == Related Facilities == * '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada Imahoricho, Joyo City) - Houses and exhibits burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun. == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|Sources used for article composition}} * Historic Site Description Board. * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2007|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun|title={{PDFlink|[http://www.kyotofu-maibun.or.jp/data/kankou/kankou-pdf/jyouhou/J104.pdf Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104]}}|publisher=Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Research Center|isbn=|pages=36-37|ref={{Harvid|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007}}}}. == Related Literature == {{small|References not used for article composition}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=Seigo Wada|year=1989|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[Tōkyōdō Shu11an]]|isbn=4490102607|ref=}}. * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1987|chapter=|title=Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo City Archaeological Report No. 16)|publisher=Joyo City Board of Education|isbn=|ref=}}. * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2014|chapter=|title=Shibagahara Kofun Excavation and Preservation Report (Joyo City Archaeological Report No. 68)|publisher=Joyo City Board of Education|isbn=|ref=}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo)}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} of Kyoto Prefecture]] {{draft categories| }} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kutsukawa Kofun Group]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Joyo]] [[Category:Zenpō-kōhō-fun]] [[Category:[[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] [[Category:National Historic Sites of Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Shiba-Gahara Kofun]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] }} [[sn:Shibagahara Kofun]] [[ja:芝ヶ原古墳]] [[sn:hibagahara Kofun]]

{{日本の古墳 |名称 = 芝ヶ原古墳 |画像 = [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|280px]]
墳丘
（右に後方部・くびれ部、左の道路部分に前方部欠失部） |別名 = 芝ケ原古墳/芝ヶ原12号墳 |所属 = [[久津川古墳群]]（芝ヶ原古墳群） |所在地 = [[京都府]][[城陽市]]寺田大谷 |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 51|緯度秒 = 45.89 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 47|経度秒 = 0.81 |ISO = JP-26 |形状 = [[前方後方墳]] |規模 = |築造時期 = [[3世紀]]中頃 |埋葬施設 = 組合式木棺直葬 |被葬者 = |出土品 = 副葬品多数・庄内式土器 |史跡 = 国の[[史跡]]「芝ヶ原古墳」 |有形文化財 = 出土品（国の[[重要文化財]]） |特記事項 = |地図 = Japan Kyoto |ラベル = 芝ヶ原古墳 |アイコン = 前方後方墳-南 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''芝ヶ原古墳'''（しばがはらこふん、芝ケ原古墳/芝ヶ原12号墳）は、[[京都府]][[城陽市]]寺田大谷にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後方墳]]。[[久津川古墳群]]（うち芝ヶ原古墳群）を構成する古墳の1つ。国の[[史跡]]に指定され、出土品は国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。 == 概要 == 京都府南部、城陽市北部の丘陵上に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。一帯では[[久津川車塚古墳]]を始めとする[[久津川古墳群]]が分布し、その支群の芝ヶ原古墳群を構成する古墳の1つ（芝ヶ原12号墳）になる{{Sfn|芝ヶ原古墳（国指定史跡）}}。[[1986年]]（[[昭和]]61年）に宅地開発に先立つ発掘調査が実施され{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}、現在は史跡公園として整備されている。 墳形は前方後方形であるが、前方部は現在までに削平されている（残存長は21メートル）{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。墳丘の段築は認められておらず、墳丘外表で[[葺石]]は認められていない{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。また墳丘周囲には周溝が巡らされる{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。埋葬施設は組合式木棺の直葬で、木棺は長さ3メートル・幅0.8メートル{{Sfn|芝ヶ原古墳（国指定史跡）}}、木棺を埋納した土壙は長さ4.7メートル・幅2.5メートルを測る{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。木棺内からは、銅鏡・銅釧・玉など多数の副葬品が検出されており{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}、特に銅釧の出土は類例のない珍しい例になる。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]初頭の[[3世紀]]中頃[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 国指定の史跡・重要文化財 > 芝ケ原古墳]（城陽市観光協会）。（または3世紀前半頃[http://www.kyoto-be.ne.jp/joyou-be/cms/?action=common_download_main&upload_id=373 史跡 芝ヶ原古墳]（城陽市教育委員会）。）の築造と推定される。南山城地方では[[椿井大塚山古墳]]に先行し、当時としては一帯で最有力の首長墓の1つに位置づけられる{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。 古墳域は[[1989年]]（[[平成]]元年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定され、出土品は[[1990年]]（平成2年）に国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。なお、[[2016年]]（平成28年）には久津川車塚古墳などの古墳4基を包括する国の史跡「久津川古墳群」が指定されたが{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf 「史跡等の指定等について」]}}（文化庁記者発表、2016年6月17日）。平成28年10月3日文部科学省告示第144号。、本古墳はこれには含まれていない。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1986年]]（[[昭和]]61年）6-8月、発掘調査（城陽市教育委員会）。 * [[1989年]]（[[平成]]元年）9月6日、国の[[史跡]]に指定。 * = [[3世紀]]中頃 |埋葬施設 = 組合式木棺直葬 |被葬者 = |出土品 = 副葬品多数・庄内式土器 |史跡 = 国の[[史跡]]「芝ヶ原古墳」 |有形文化財 = 出土品（国の[[重要文化財]]） |特記事項 = |地図 = Japan Kyoto |ラベル = 芝ヶ原古墳 |アイコン = 前方後方墳-南 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''芝ヶ原古墳'''（しばがはらこふん、芝ケ原古墳/芝ヶ原12号墳）は、[[京都府]][[城陽市]]寺田大谷にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後方墳]]。[[久津川古墳群]]（うち芝ヶ原古墳群）を構成する古墳の1つ。国の[[史跡]]に指定され、出土品は国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。 == 概要 == 京都府南部、城陽市北部の丘陵上に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。一帯では[[久津川車塚古墳]]を始めとする[[久津川古墳群]]が分布し、その支群の芝ヶ原古墳群を構成する古墳の1つ（芝ヶ原12号墳）になる{{Sfn|芝ヶ原古墳（国指定史跡）}}。[[1986年]]（[[昭和]]61年）に宅地開発に先立つ発掘調査が実施され{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}、現在は史跡公園として整備されている。 墳形は前方後方形であるが、前方部は現在までに削平されている（残存長は21メートル）{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。墳丘の段築は認められておらず、墳丘外表で[[葺石]]は認められていない{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。また墳丘周囲には周溝が巡らされる{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。埋葬施設は組合式木棺の直葬で、木棺は長さ3メートル・幅0.8メートル{{Sfn|芝ヶ原古墳（国指定史跡）}}、木棺を埋納した土壙は長さ4.7メートル・幅2.5メートルを測る{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。木棺内からは、銅鏡・銅釧・玉など多数の副葬品が検出されており{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}、特に銅釧の出土は類例のない珍しい例になる。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]初頭の[[3世紀]]中頃[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 国指定の史跡・重要文化財 > 芝ケ原古墳]（城陽市観光協会）。（または3世紀前半頃[http://www.kyoto-be.ne.jp/joyou-be/cms/?action=common_download_main&upload_id=373 史跡 芝ヶ原古墳]（城陽市教育委員会）。）の築造と推定される。南山城地方では[[椿井大塚山古墳]]に先行し、当時としては一帯で最有力の首長墓の1つに位置づけられる{{Sfn|京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第104号|2007|pp=36-37}}。 古墳域は[[1989年]]（[[平成]]元年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定され、出土品は[[1990年]]（平成2年）に国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。なお、[[2016年]]（平成28年）には久津川車塚古墳などの古墳4基を包括する国の史跡「久津川古墳群」が指定されたが{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Mound
(Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | Historic Site = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | omitted = 前方後方墳-南 | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | Historic Site = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | omitted = 前方後方墳-南 | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Group|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). (Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joyo, Kyoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | Historic Site = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | omitted = 前方後方墳-南 | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joyo, Kyoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|qq=}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|qq=}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' - Designated June 29, 1990{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}. === National Historic Site === * '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}. == Related Facilities == * '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada Imahoricho, Joyo (Right: rear mound; Left: missing front mound part, now a road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | part_of = {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (Shibagahara Kofun Cluster) | location = Terada Ōtani, Jōyō, Kyoto Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} | area = | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Directly buried in composite wooden coffin | Interred_individual = Unknown | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōnai-style pottery|qq=}} | notes = National Historic Site | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} | special_notes = | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | type = Keyhole tomb with square mounds, facing south | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} Kofun located in Terada Ōtani, {{ill|Jōyō, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōyō, Kyoto|qq=}}, Kyoto Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} and types part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. This kofun has been Historic Site1 a National Historic Site, and its excavated burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was built atop a hill in the northern part of Jōyō City, southern Kyoto Prefecture. It is part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, specifically the Shibagahara subgroup (Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun). An excavation in 1986 preceded the area's residential development, and the site has since been maintained as a historical park.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. This tomb is a keyhole-shaped mound with square front and rear mounds; however, the front portion has been leveled (current remaining length: 21 meters).{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The mound shows no signs of terracing, nor does it feature any {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}}. Surrounding the mound is a {{ill|moat|ja|周溝|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/moat|qq=}}.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin buried directly in the ground. The coffin measures 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width, while the burial pit is 4.7 meters long and 2.5 meters wide.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Numerous grave goods, including a {{ill|bronze mirror|ja|銅鏡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/bronze mirror|qq=}}, bronze bracelets, and jewels, were recovered from the coffin. Among these, the bronze bracelets are particularly rare examples.{{Harvid|Joyo City Official Page}}. The tomb was constructed in the mid-3rd century (or the early 3rd century according to some sources) during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}. It predates the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|qq=}} and is considered one of the most significant Kofuns of its era in the southern Yamashiro region.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The kofun was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989, with its grave goods receiving National Important designation1 status in 1990. In 2016, the broader {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, encompassing four additional kofun, was also Historic Site1 a National Historic Site.{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf "Regarding the designation1 of Historic Sites"]}} (Agency of Cultural Affairs press release, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Notice No. 144, October 3, 2016. However, Shibagahara Kofun itself is not included in this extended Historic Site. == Archaeological History == * 1986 (Shōwa 61): Excavation by the Jōyō City Board of Education. * 1989 (Heisei 1): Designated a National Historic Site on September 6. * 1990 (Heisei 2): burial goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} on June 29. * 2012 (Heisei 24): Additional area Historic Site1 as part of the historic site. == Mound area == The mound’s area are as follows:{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Rear mound ** North-south: 21 meters ** East-west: 19 meters * Front mound ** Length: Approximately 3.5 meters * Neck portion ** Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Four-animal mirror}}{{small|Exhibited at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze bracelet}}]] Key burial goods recovered from the wooden coffin include:{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Four-animal bronze mirror (仿製鏡) – Diameter: 12 cm * Two bronze bracelets (同笵) * Eight jadeite magatama * 187 jasper tubular beads * 1,276 glass beads * One yari-ganna (adze) Additionally, fragments of {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōnai-style pottery|qq=}}, including double-rimmed jars and high-footed bowls, were found in the gravel layer above the burial pit.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}} These burial goods are preserved and displayed at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum. File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 装身具.JPG|Ornaments File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 庄内式土器.JPG|Shōnai-style pottery == designation1 designation1s == === Important designation1 (National) === * burial goods excavated from Shibagahara Kofun – Includes bronze bracelets, bronze mirror, magatama, tubular beads, glass beads, iron chisels, and pottery fragments. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{designation1 Database|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shibagahara Kofun – Designated on September 6, 1989, with additional area Historic Site1 in 2012.{{designation1 Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} == Related Facilities == * Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum (Gorigorikan) – Terada Imahoru, Jōyō City; houses and displays burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|title=Archaeological Intypeation, Vol. 104|editor=Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Research Center|year=2007|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun|pages=36–37}} * {{Cite book|title=National Historic Sites Guide|editor=Kodansha|year=2016|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun}} == External Links == * {{Commonscat|Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo)}} * {{designation1 Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|芝ヶ原古墳|version=99994934|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Jōyō]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:National Historic Sites in Kyoto]] [[Category:Completion tier 3]] [[Category:Shibagahara Kofun Group]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property (Japan)]] [[sn:Shibagahara Kofun Group]][[sn:Shibagahara Kofun Group]]}} [[sn:Shibagahara Kofun Group]] [[ja:芝ヶ原古墳]] [[Category:Merged pages]]

(Right: rear section and constricted section, Left: missing front section along the road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | location = {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joyo, Kyoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan | coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark}} | type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Direct burial in a composite wooden coffin | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, Shōnai-style pottery | Historic Site = National Historic Site (Shibagahara Kofun) | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National Important Cultural Property | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | omitted = 前方後方墳-南 | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} located in {{ill|Joyo, Kyoto|ja|城陽市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joyo, Kyoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|qq=}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|qq=}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: A11roximately 3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' - Designated June 29, 1990{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}. === National Historic Site === * '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}. == Related Facilities == * '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada Imahoricho, Joyo
