(Right: rear mound; Left: missing front mound part, now a road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | part_of = {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (Shibagahara Kofun Cluster) | location = Terada Ōtani, Jōyō, Kyoto Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | area = | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Directly buried in composite wooden coffin | Interred_individual = Unknown | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōnai-style pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | notes = National Historic Site | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} | special_notes = | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | type = Keyhole tomb with square mounds, facing south | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} Kofun located in Terada Ōtani, {{ill|Jōyō, Kyoto|en|Jōyō, Kyoto|WD=Q817276|lt=Jōyō, Kyoto|1=Jōyō, Kyoto}}, Kyoto Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and types part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. This kofun has been Historic Site1 a National Historic Site, and its excavated burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was built atop a hill in the northern part of Jōyō City, southern Kyoto Prefecture. It is part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, specifically the Shibagahara subgroup (Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun). An excavation in 1986 preceded the area's residential development, and the site has since been maintained as a historical park.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. This tomb is a keyhole-shaped mound with square front and rear mounds; however, the front portion has been leveled (current remaining length: 21 meters).{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The mound shows no signs of terracing, nor does it feature any {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}}. Surrounding the mound is a {{ill|moat|ja|周溝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/moat|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin buried directly in the ground. The coffin measures 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width, while the burial pit is 4.7 meters long and 2.5 meters wide.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Numerous grave goods, including a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=bronze mirror|1=Bronze mirror}}, bronze bracelets, and jewels, were recovered from the coffin. Among these, the bronze bracelets are particularly rare examples.{{Harvid|Joyo City Official Page}}. The tomb was constructed in the mid-3rd century (or the early 3rd century according to some sources) during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}. It predates the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} and is considered one of the most significant Kofuns of its era in the southern Yamashiro region.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The kofun was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989, with its grave goods receiving National Important designation1 status in 1990. In 2016, the broader {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, encompassing four additional kofun, was also Historic Site1 a National Historic Site.{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf "Regarding the designation1 of Historic Sites"]}} (Agency of Cultural Affairs press release, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Notice No. 144, October 3, 2016. However, Shibagahara Kofun itself is not included in this extended Historic Site. == Archaeological History == * 1986 (Shōwa 61): Excavation by the Jōyō City Board of Education. * 1989 (Heisei 1): Designated a National Historic Site on September 6. * 1990 (Heisei 2): burial goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} on June 29. * 2012 (Heisei 24): Additional area Historic Site1 as part of the historic site. == Mound area == The mound’s area are as follows:{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Rear mound ** North-south: 21 meters ** East-west: 19 meters * Front mound ** Length: Approximately 3.5 meters * Neck portion ** Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Four-animal mirror}}{{small|Exhibited at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze bracelet}}]] Key burial goods recovered from the wooden coffin include:{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Four-animal bronze mirror (仿製鏡) – Diameter: 12 cm * Two bronze bracelets (同笵) * Eight jadeite magatama * 187 jasper tubular beads * 1,276 glass beads * One yari-ganna (adze) Additionally, fragments of {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōnai-style pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including double-rimmed jars and high-footed bowls, were found in the gravel layer above the burial pit.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}} These burial goods are preserved and displayed at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{designation1 Database|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shibagahara Kofun – Designated on September 6, 1989, with additional area Historic Site1 in 2012.{{designation1 Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} == Related Facilities == * Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum (Gorigorikan) – Terada Imahoru, Jōyō City; houses and displays burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|title=Archaeological Intypeation, Vol. 104|editor=Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Research Center|year=2007|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun|pages=36–37}} * {{Cite book|title=National Historic Sites Guide|editor=Kodansha|year=2016|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun}} == External Links == * {{Commonscat|Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo)}} * {{designation1 Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|芝ヶ原古墳|version=99994934|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:芝ヶ原古墳]] {{Commons category|Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo)}} [[en:Shibagahara Kofun]] {{wikidata link|Q28608915}} [[Category:{{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} [[Category:Completion tier 3]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Kyoto prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Kyoto prefecture]] [[Category:Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Shikinaisha merges]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Zenpō-kōhō-fun]] [[Category:pages]]

It is a {{ill|keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and types part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. This kofun has been Historic Site1 a National Historic Site, and its excavated burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was built atop a hill in the northern part of Jōyō City, southern Kyoto Prefecture. It is part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, specifically the Shibagahara subgroup (Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun). An excavation in 1986 preceded the area's residential development, and the site has since been maintained as a historical park.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. This tomb is a keyhole-shaped mound with square front and rear mounds; however, the front portion has been leveled (current remaining length: 21 meters).{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The mound shows no signs of terracing, nor does it feature any {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}}. Surrounding the mound is a {{ill|moat|ja|周溝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/moat|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin buried directly in the ground. The coffin measures 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width, while the burial pit is 4.7 meters long and 2.5 meters wide.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Numerous grave goods, including a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=bronze mirror|1=Bronze mirror}}, bronze bracelets, and jewels, were recovered from the coffin. Among these, the bronze bracelets are particularly rare examples.{{Harvid|Joyo City Official Page}}. The tomb was constructed in the mid-3rd century (or the early 3rd century according to some sources) during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}. It predates the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} and is considered one of the most significant Kofuns of its era in the southern Yamashiro region.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The kofun was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989, with its grave goods receiving National Important designation1 status in 1990. In 2016, the broader {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, encompassing four additional kofun, was also Historic Site1 a National Historic Site.{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf "Regarding the designation1 of Historic Sites"]}} (Agency of Cultural Affairs press release, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Notice No. 144, October 3, 2016. However, Shibagahara Kofun itself is not included in this extended Historic Site. == Archaeological History == * 1986 (Shōwa 61): Excavation by the Jōyō City Board of Education. * 1989 (Heisei 1): Designated a National Historic Site on September 6. * 1990 (Heisei 2): burial goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} on June 29. * 2012 (Heisei 24): Additional area Historic Site1 as part of the historic site. == Mound area == The mound’s area are as follows:{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Rear mound ** North-south: 21 meters ** East-west: 19 meters * Front mound ** Length: Approximately 3.5 meters * Neck portion ** Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Four-animal mirror}}{{small|Exhibited at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze bracelet}}]] Key burial goods recovered from the wooden coffin include:{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Four-animal bronze mirror (仿製鏡) – Diameter: 12 cm * Two bronze bracelets (同笵) * Eight jadeite magatama * 187 jasper tubular beads * 1,276 glass beads * One yari-ganna (adze) Additionally, fragments of {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōnai-style pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including double-rimmed jars and high-footed bowls, were found in the gravel layer above the burial pit.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}} These burial goods are preserved and displayed at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum. '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in Kyoto|1=Jōyō, Kyoto}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|WD=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture|1=Kyoto Prefecture}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|1=Kutsukawa Kurumazuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11369464}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: Approximately3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). It is a {{ill|keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and types part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. This kofun has been Historic Site1 a National Historic Site, and its excavated burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was built atop a hill in the northern part of Jōyō City, southern Kyoto Prefecture. It is part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, specifically the Shibagahara subgroup (Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun). An excavation in 1986 preceded the area's residential development, and the site has since been maintained as a historical park.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. This tomb is a keyhole-shaped mound with square front and rear mounds; however, the front portion has been leveled (current remaining length: 21 meters).{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The mound shows no signs of terracing, nor does it feature any {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}}. Surrounding the mound is a {{ill|moat|ja|周溝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/moat|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin buried directly in the ground. The coffin measures 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width, while the burial pit is 4.7 meters long and 2.5 meters wide.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Numerous grave goods, including a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=bronze mirror|1=Bronze mirror}}, bronze bracelets, and jewels, were recovered from the coffin. Among these, the bronze bracelets are particularly rare examples.{{Harvid|Joyo City Official Page}}. The tomb was constructed in the mid-3rd century (or the early 3rd century according to some sources) during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}. It predates the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} and is considered one of the most significant Kofuns of its era in the southern Yamashiro region.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The kofun was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989, with its grave goods receiving National Important designation1 status in 1990. In 2016, the broader {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, encompassing four additional kofun, was also Historic Site1 a National Historic Site.{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf "Regarding the designation1 of Historic Sites"]}} (Agency of Cultural Affairs press release, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Notice No. 144, October 3, 2016. However, Shibagahara Kofun itself is not included in this extended Historic Site. == Archaeological History == * 1986 (Shōwa 61): Excavation by the Jōyō City Board of Education. * 1989 (Heisei 1): Designated a National Historic Site on September 6. * 1990 (Heisei 2): burial goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} on June 29. * 2012 (Heisei 24): Additional area Historic Site1 as part of the historic site. == Mound area == The mound’s area are as follows:{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Rear mound ** North-south: 21 meters ** East-west: 19 meters * Front mound ** Length: Approximately 3.5 meters * Neck portion ** Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Four-animal mirror}}{{small|Exhibited at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze bracelet}}]] Key burial goods recovered from the wooden coffin include:{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Four-animal bronze mirror (仿製鏡) – Diameter: 12 cm * Two bronze bracelets (同笵) * Eight jadeite magatama * 187 jasper tubular beads * 1,276 glass beads * One yari-ganna (adze) Additionally, fragments of {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōnai-style pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including double-rimmed jars and high-footed bowls, were found in the gravel layer above the burial pit.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}} These burial goods are preserved and displayed at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum. '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in Kyoto|1=Jōyō, Kyoto}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|WD=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture|1=Kyoto Prefecture}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|1=Kutsukawa Kurumazuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11369464}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: Approximately3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in Kyoto|1=Jōyō, Kyoto}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|WD=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture|1=Kyoto Prefecture}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|1=Kutsukawa Kurumazuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11369464}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: Approximately3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). It is part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, specifically the Shibagahara subgroup (Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun). An excavation in 1986 preceded the area's residential development, and the site has since been maintained as a historical park.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. This tomb is a keyhole-shaped mound with square front and rear mounds; however, the front portion has been leveled (current remaining length: 21 meters).{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The mound shows no signs of terracing, nor does it feature any {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}}. Surrounding the mound is a {{ill|moat|ja|周溝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/moat|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin buried directly in the ground. The coffin measures 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width, while the burial pit is 4.7 meters long and 2.5 meters wide.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Numerous grave goods, including a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=bronze mirror|1=Bronze mirror}}, bronze bracelets, and jewels, were recovered from the coffin. Among these, the bronze bracelets are particularly rare examples.{{Harvid|Joyo City Official Page}}. The tomb was constructed in the mid-3rd century (or the early 3rd century according to some sources) during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}. The kofun was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989, with its grave goods receiving National Important designation1 status in 1990. In 2016, the broader {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, encompassing four additional kofun, was also Historic Site1 a National Historic Site.{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf "Regarding the designation1 of Historic Sites"]}} (Agency of Cultural Affairs press release, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Notice No. 144, October 3, 2016. '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} located in {{ill|Jōyō, Kyoto|en|Jōyō, Kyoto|WD=Q817276|lt=Joyo, Kyoto|1=Jōyō, Kyoto}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|WD=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture|1=Kyoto Prefecture}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|1=Kutsukawa Kurumazuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11369464}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: Approximately3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). Designated June 29, 1990{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}. === National Historic Site === * '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}. == Related Facilities == * '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada Imahoricho, Joyo City) - Houses and exhibits burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun. == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|Sources used for article composition}} * Historic Site Description Board. * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2007|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun|title={{PDFlink|[http://www.kyotofu-maibun.or.jp/data/kankou/kankou-pdf/jyouhou/J104.pdf Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104]}}|publisher=Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Research Center|isbn=|pages=36-37|ref={{Harvid|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007}}}}. == Related Literature == {{small|References not used for article composition}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=Seigo Wada|year=1989|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[Tōkyōdō Shu11an]]|isbn=4490102607|ref=}}. * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1987|chapter=|title=Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo City Archaeological Report No. 16)|publisher=Joyo City Board of Education|isbn=|ref=}}. * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2014|chapter=|title=Shibagahara Kofun Excavation and Preservation Report (Joyo City Archaeological Report No. 68)|publisher=Joyo City Board of Education|isbn=|ref=}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo)}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} of Kyoto Prefecture]] {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|芝ヶ原古墳|version=99994934|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:芝ヶ原古墳]] [[Category:Pages with duplicated content]] ==Merged second translation== {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Shibagahara Kofun (芝ヶ原古墳) | image = [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|280px]]

(Right: rear mound; Left: missing front mound part, now a road) | alternate_name = Shibagahara Kofun/Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun | part_of = {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (Shibagahara Kofun Cluster) | location = Terada Ōtani, Jōyō, Kyoto Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|51|45.89|N|135|47|0.81|E|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | area = | built = Mid-3rd century | burial = Directly buried in composite wooden coffin | Interred_individual = Unknown | burial goods = Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōnai-style pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | notes = National Historic Site | notes = burial goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} | special_notes = | map = Japan Kyoto | map_dot_label = Shibagahara Kofun | type = Keyhole tomb with square mounds, facing south | map_dot_label = top }} '''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} Kofun located in Terada Ōtani, {{ill|Jōyō, Kyoto|en|Jōyō, Kyoto|WD=Q817276|lt=Jōyō, Kyoto|1=Jōyō, Kyoto}}, Kyoto Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and types part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. This kofun has been Historic Site1 a National Historic Site, and its excavated burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was built atop a hill in the northern part of Jōyō City, southern Kyoto Prefecture. It is part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, specifically the Shibagahara subgroup (Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun). An excavation in 1986 preceded the area's residential development, and the site has since been maintained as a historical park.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. This tomb is a keyhole-shaped mound with square front and rear mounds; however, the front portion has been leveled (current remaining length: 21 meters).{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The mound shows no signs of terracing, nor does it feature any {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}}. Surrounding the mound is a {{ill|moat|ja|周溝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/moat|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin buried directly in the ground. The coffin measures 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width, while the burial pit is 4.7 meters long and 2.5 meters wide.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Numerous grave goods, including a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=bronze mirror|1=Bronze mirror}}, bronze bracelets, and jewels, were recovered from the coffin. Among these, the bronze bracelets are particularly rare examples.{{Harvid|Joyo City Official Page}}. The tomb was constructed in the mid-3rd century (or the early 3rd century according to some sources) during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}. It predates the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} and is considered one of the most significant Kofuns of its era in the southern Yamashiro region.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The kofun was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989, with its grave goods receiving National Important designation1 status in 1990. In 2016, the broader {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, encompassing four additional kofun, was also Historic Site1 a National Historic Site.{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf "Regarding the designation1 of Historic Sites"]}} (Agency of Cultural Affairs press release, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Notice No. 144, October 3, 2016. However, Shibagahara Kofun itself is not included in this extended Historic Site. == Archaeological History == * 1986 (Shōwa 61): Excavation by the Jōyō City Board of Education. * 1989 (Heisei 1): Designated a National Historic Site on September 6. * 1990 (Heisei 2): burial goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} on June 29. * 2012 (Heisei 24): Additional area Historic Site1 as part of the historic site. == Mound area == The mound’s area are as follows:{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Rear mound ** North-south: 21 meters ** East-west: 19 meters * Front mound ** Length: Approximately 3.5 meters * Neck portion ** Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Four-animal mirror}}{{small|Exhibited at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze bracelet}}]] Key burial goods recovered from the wooden coffin include:{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Four-animal bronze mirror (仿製鏡) – Diameter: 12 cm * Two bronze bracelets (同笵) * Eight jadeite magatama * 187 jasper tubular beads * 1,276 glass beads * One yari-ganna (adze) Additionally, fragments of {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōnai-style pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including double-rimmed jars and high-footed bowls, were found in the gravel layer above the burial pit.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}} These burial goods are preserved and displayed at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{designation1 Database|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shibagahara Kofun – Designated on September 6, 1989, with additional area Historic Site1 in 2012.{{designation1 Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} == Related Facilities == * Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum (Gorigorikan) – Terada Imahoru, Jōyō City; houses and displays burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|title=Archaeological Intypeation, Vol. 104|editor=Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Research Center|year=2007|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun|pages=36–37}} * {{Cite book|title=National Historic Sites Guide|editor=Kodansha|year=2016|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun}} == External Links == * {{Commonscat|Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo)}} * {{designation1 Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|芝ヶ原古墳|version=99994934|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:芝ヶ原古墳]] {{Commons category|Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo)}} [[en:Shibagahara Kofun]] {{wikidata link|Q28608915}} [[Category:{{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Kyoto prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Kyoto prefecture]] [[Category:Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Pages with duplicated content]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Zenpō-kōhō-fun]]

kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} located in {{ill|Jōyō, Kyoto|en|Jōyō, Kyoto|WD=Q817276|lt=Joyo, Kyoto|1=Jōyō, Kyoto}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|WD=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture|1=Kyoto Prefecture}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|1=Kutsukawa Kurumazuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11369464}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park. While originally a {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique. The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1) and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in 1990 (Heisei 2). == Excavation History == * '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education. * '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6. * '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} on June 29. * '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries. == Mound Details == [[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]] The mound's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Rear section''' ''' North-South: 21 meters ''' East-West: 19 meters * '''Front section''' ''' Length: Approximately3.5 meters * '''Constricted section''' ''' Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]] Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}: * '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror). * '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set). * '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces. * '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces. * '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces. * '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece. Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan). It is a {{ill|keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole tomb with square front and back mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and types part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. This kofun has been Historic Site1 a National Historic Site, and its excavated burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. == Overview == Shibagahara Kofun was built atop a hill in the northern part of Jōyō City, southern Kyoto Prefecture. It is part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, specifically the Shibagahara subgroup (Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun). An excavation in 1986 preceded the area's residential development, and the site has since been maintained as a historical park.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. This tomb is a keyhole-shaped mound with square front and rear mounds; however, the front portion has been leveled (current remaining length: 21 meters).{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The mound shows no signs of terracing, nor does it feature any {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}}. Surrounding the mound is a {{ill|moat|ja|周溝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/moat|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin buried directly in the ground. The coffin measures 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width, while the burial pit is 4.7 meters long and 2.5 meters wide.{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Numerous grave goods, including a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=bronze mirror|1=Bronze mirror}}, bronze bracelets, and jewels, were recovered from the coffin. Among these, the bronze bracelets are particularly rare examples.{{Harvid|Joyo City Official Page}}. The tomb was constructed in the mid-3rd century (or the early 3rd century according to some sources) during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}. It predates the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} and is considered one of the most significant Kofuns of its era in the southern Yamashiro region.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}. The kofun was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989, with its grave goods receiving National Important designation1 status in 1990. In 2016, the broader {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, encompassing four additional kofun, was also Historic Site1 a National Historic Site.{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf "Regarding the designation1 of Historic Sites"]}} (Agency of Cultural Affairs press release, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Notice No. 144, October 3, 2016. However, Shibagahara Kofun itself is not included in this extended Historic Site. == Archaeological History == * 1986 (Shōwa 61): Excavation by the Jōyō City Board of Education. * 1989 (Heisei 1): Designated a National Historic Site on September 6. * 1990 (Heisei 2): burial goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} on June 29. * 2012 (Heisei 24): Additional area Historic Site1 as part of the historic site. == Mound area == The mound’s area are as follows:{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Rear mound ** North-south: 21 meters ** East-west: 19 meters * Front mound ** Length: Approximately 3.5 meters * Neck portion ** Width: 11.6 meters == burial goods == [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Four-animal mirror}}{{small|Exhibited at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] [[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze bracelet}}]] Key burial goods recovered from the wooden coffin include:{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. * Four-animal bronze mirror (仿製鏡) – Diameter: 12 cm * Two bronze bracelets (同笵) * Eight jadeite magatama * 187 jasper tubular beads * 1,276 glass beads * One yari-ganna (adze) Additionally, fragments of {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōnai-style pottery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including double-rimmed jars and high-footed bowls, were found in the gravel layer above the burial pit.{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}} These burial goods are preserved and displayed at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{designation1 Database|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shibagahara Kofun – Designated on September 6, 1989, with additional area Historic Site1 in 2012.{{designation1 Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} == Related Facilities == * Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum (Gorigorikan) – Terada Imahoru, Jōyō City; houses and displays burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|title=Archaeological Intypeation, Vol. 104|editor=Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Research Center|year=2007|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun|pages=36–37}} * {{Cite book|title=National Historic Sites Guide|editor=Kodansha|year=2016|chapter=Shibagahara Kofun}} == External Links == * {{Commonscat|Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo)}} * {{designation1 Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|芝ヶ原古墳|version=99994934|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:芝ヶ原古墳]] {{Commons category|Shibagahara Kofun (Joyo)}} [[en:Shibagahara Kofun]] {{wikidata link|Q28608915}} [[Category:{{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Kyoto prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Kyoto prefecture]] [[Category:Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Pages with duplicated content]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Zenpō-kōhō-fun]]
